title: Staged safety-net deployer for autonomous cost advice
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Optimize suggests batching and KV-cache profile changes that can materially lower token cost but risk increasing p95 latency or introducing regression for some routes. Current autopilot can apply suggestions but lacks a lightweight staged verification runway and operator-facing veto/visibility model. Goal: implement a staged safety-net deployer that vets Optimize recommendations through simulation, dark-launch canaries, telemetry gates, and an approval escalation path before committing changes cluster-wide. The feature must support automatic rollback triggers, operator overrides, and an audit trail for compliance teams.

Proposed approach:
1) Vetting simulation: run suggestion through a simulator using recent traffic traces (sampled across routes and models) to estimate latency percentile impact and token savings. Produce a per-route risk score and deterministic delta metrics.
2) Staged dark-launch: implement a dark-launch mode where the recommended config is applied to a shadow path that observes live traffic but does not affect responses (collecting latency, error, and model divergence signals).
3) Canary cohorts: route a small % of real traffic to the new config for a limited set of robust routes (tiered by SLA and traffic volume). Canary gradually expands using pause-and-evaluate gates.
4) Telemetry safety gates: define thresholds for p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, model-quality regressions (based on eval prompts), and throughput. Gate evaluation runs after each expansion window; violations trigger automatic rollback to previous config.
5) Approval workflow: add an optional operator approval step between simulation and canary. For fully-autonomous mode, require pre-configured risk tolerances; for operator-assisted mode, surface a concise decision card in Console with suggested rollout and test results.
6) Audit & revert: log events to the private audit stream with commit metadata, user decisions, and observed telemetry snapshots. Provide a one-click revert that can roll configs back at route granularity.
7) Safety playbook: author an ops playbook that includes investigation steps, escalation contacts, and mitigation commands for common failure modes (latency spikes, error surge, quality regressions).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator produces per-suggestion risk report and estimated cost delta within 10% of observed post-apply after canary completes
Dark-launch pipeline can ingest 1% sampled traffic across top 50 routes without affecting response paths
Canary controller supports 3 expansion phases (0.1%, 1%, 5%) with automatic pause-if-gate-fails and metrics windowing configurable per-project
Rollback triggers execute within 30s of gate violation detection and revert route-level config to last-known-good
Console shows a decision card with simulation summary, canary status, and a timeline of events; approvals recorded in audit logs
Ops playbook published and linked from the Console decision card
tasks: Design simulation service API and sample-store integration (design doc + cost estimates)
Implement dark-launch proxy hook and shadow telemetry pipeline
Build canary controller with expansion + pause logic and reusable gate evaluators
Define default gate thresholds and wire to telemetry ingestion (tracing + metrics + eval checks)
Add Console UI decision card and approval flow (approve/reject/override with reason)
Add audit events, immutable commit metadata, and one-click revert plumbing
Write end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (latency spike, model divergence)
Author ops playbook and run a simulated incident drill with SRE
